questions.prompt: What part of a recursive function makes it terminate?

options.text: The base case, which returns directly without recursing

questions.explanation: The base case stops the recursion. Without a reachable base case, calls continue until Python raises RecursionError.

questions.prompt: What does the runtime use to keep track of pending (not-yet-returned) function calls?

options.text: The call stack, pushing a frame per call

questions.explanation: Each call pushes a stack frame with its locals and return point; the frame is popped when the call returns. Depth = stack space used.

questions.prompt: Which statements about recursion in Python are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Each recursive call adds a frame to the call stack
A missing or unreachable base case leads to infinite recursion (RecursionError)
Naive recursive Fibonacci runs in exponential time
CPython optimizes tail calls so tail recursion uses O(1) stack

questions.explanation: Frames stack up, a bad base case never stops, and naive Fibonacci is exponential. CPython has NO tail-call optimization, so (d) is false.

questions.prompt: The naive recursive Fibonacci runs in ______ time (name the growth class in one word).
questions.explanation: It recomputes overlapping subproblems, giving Θ(φⁿ) ≈ exponential growth; memoization reduces it to linear.

questions.prompt: In evaluating factorial(3), order the calls by when they RETURN (first to return first).
questions.explanation: The recursion descends to the base case, which returns first; the stack then unwinds outward, so factorial(3) returns last.

questions.prompt: Match each term with its meaning.

pairs.right: Returns directly and stops the recursion
Reduces the input and calls itself
Holds a frame per pending call

questions.explanation: These are the core recursion concepts: the two cases, where calls live, and the space cost.
